answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent is a vertex in the trust graph, but it only becomes a live vertex after posting a hashed commitment to a public river of entries and waiting a fixed number of epochs before revealing the key behind it. A Sybil attacker who wants a thousand identities must pay the anchor fee a thousand times up front and sit through the delay for each one, so fake agents cannot arrive like a comet in a single burst; they trickle in slowly and visibly, giving peers time to flag clustered commitments before any of them can vote or earn.
